content.comment_body: Hello, I have a program for controlling my garage heating ([article_no]). Using a potentiometer, I set the desired temperature with an analog threshold trigger block. PI and PWM blocks manage the heater's on/off actions and everything works well. I can connect to the [product_name] via the internet to check the hour counter and current setpoint. My question: Is there a way to adjust the input value remotely? I'd like to connect to the [product_name] online and change the setpoint. For example, if the potentiometer is at 8 degrees, I'd want to change it to 12 degrees using my phone. Is this possible? My program is attached. Regards

Since you've set up the message text for the web server, and already access the [product_name] via Ethernet, you can use your internet-enabled phone to reach the web server and modify the setpoint temperature.

I've updated your program so it allows setpoint changes through the display, removing the need for the analog input with the potentiometer. This lets you adjust the setpoint using the web server interface. Review the video for details.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are interested in adjusting the temperature setpoint on a [product_name] device for garage heating remotely, potentially through a smartphone. Current visibility via the web server exists, but users want the ability to change setpoints online, especially if analog input is excluded from the control loop. Remote parameter changes using common devices are appreciated by users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to change the garage heating temperature setpoint remotely through a smartphone-accessible web interface, eliminating the need for on-site adjustment via a potentiometer.
